methods.label: Use area and the outer boundary
methods.explanation:
The areas determine the square's side length even though the picture is not drawn to scale. Since the five rectangles partition the square, its area is
\[
1\cdot6+2\cdot4+5\cdot6+2\cdot7+2\cdot3=64.
\]
Thus the square has side length \(8\) and perimeter \(4\cdot8=32\).

In the displayed arrangement, each outer rectangle occupies one corner of the square. One full horizontal side and one full vertical side of that rectangle lie on the outer boundary. Its contribution to that boundary is therefore its length plus its width. These eight segments partition the square's boundary, so the sum of length plus width for the four outer rectangles is \(32\).

For all five rectangles, the corresponding sum is
\[
(1+6)+(2+4)+(5+6)+(2+7)+(2+3)=38.
\]
Therefore the middle rectangle has length plus width
\[
38-32=6.
\]
Only the \(2\times4\) rectangle has this sum. The shaded rectangle is \(\boxed{B}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
